reason: Both conversations were safe (unplug before checks, stop on burning smell or grinding) and both honestly kept the diagnosis open between jockey pulley/belt and drum rollers/bearing without declaring a definite cause. Conversation 1 covered the expected sensible first step by addressing levelling (including shims and the wooden-floor issue without lifting), gave practical standing-up ways to localise the noise front vs rear, adapted repeatedly to the customer's back injury and basic tools, and tied part advice to the known IDC8T3B model while deferring the actual fix to an engineer. Conversation 2 was accurate and appropriately escalated but never raised levelling or noise location, repeated the drum-lift check the customer couldn't do, and offered no further non-invasive checks, leaving the homeowner with less to tell the repairer. Neither ruled out the condensate pump, so that is a wash.
